title: AI-Chip & ML-Systems Engineering (GPU Kernels to Compilers)
tagline: Build the layer that makes AI fast on hardware — the highest, most durable rung of the AI-infrastructure stack.
summary: Build the layer that makes AI fast on hardware — the highest, most durable rung of the AI-infrastructure stack. You start with just enough deep learning to know what you're optimizing (tensors, GEMM, the transformer, attention, what's memory- vs compute-bound, quantization), then engineer the GPU kernels behind modern models: optimized matmul and tensor cores, softmax/LayerNorm reductions, and kernel fusion — culminating in a FlashAttention-style fused attention kernel. You then rise above hand-tuned CUDA to the layer that survives automation: Triton (block-level GPU programming in Python) and ML compilers (MLIR, TVM, torch.compile) that lower a model graph to hardware. The capstone is a fused attention kernel measured against a vendor baseline. This is Branch B of the Zero-to-Low-Level-Systems-Elite program — the path to NVIDIA, the frontier labs (the largest AI and platform companies/a frontier lab), and AI-chip startups, where the durable edge is designing the kernels and compilers, not memorizing intrinsics a model can emit.

capstone.title: Fused Attention Kernel — Optimized & Benchmarked Against a Vendor Baseline
capstone.project: Implement scaled-dot-product attention and then optimize it into a FlashAttention-style fused, tiled kernel (in CUDA and/or Triton) that computes attention without ever materializing the full N x N score matrix, using online softmax. Benchmark it for latency and memory against a naive baseline and a vendor/reference implementation (PyTorch / cuBLAS / cuDNN / FlashAttention), verify numerical correctness, and write up where the speedup and memory savings come from.

phases.title: Deep Learning for Systems Engineers
phases.goal: Learn what the hardware actually runs: tensors and GEMM, the transformer and attention, training vs inference, memory- vs compute-bound ops, and numeric precision/quantization.

projects.title: Tensors & the Shape of Computation
projects.description: Explore tensors as N-dimensional arrays with shape, strides, and dtype; understand row-major layout, contiguity, and broadcasting, and connect each concept to its GPU memory-access implication.

projects.title: GEMM: The Operation That Runs AI
projects.description: Implement matrix multiply from scratch, count FLOPs using the 2×M×N×K formula, measure GPU GEMM throughput, and identify which transformer layers dominate the FLOPs budget.

projects.title: A Neural Net Forward Pass from Scratch
projects.description: Implement a 3-layer MLP forward pass in NumPy, instrument it with FLOPs and bytes-per-layer counts, classify each op as compute-bound or memory-bound, and verify against PyTorch's nn.Sequential.

projects.title: Anatomy of a Transformer
projects.description: Implement a full transformer encoder layer from scratch in PyTorch, produce a per-component FLOPs breakdown, compute weight and activation memory, and map every sub-block to its kernel type (GEMM vs elementwise).

projects.title: The Attention Mechanism in Detail
projects.description: Implement scaled dot-product and multi-head attention from scratch in NumPy and PyTorch, apply causal masking, quantify the O(S²) memory cost, and compare standard attention to F.scaled_dot_product_attention.

projects.title: Compute-Bound vs Memory-Bound Ops
projects.description: Build a roofline calculator, compute arithmetic intensity for every major ML op, classify each as compute-bound or memory-bound, and produce a per-op optimization agenda for a full transformer layer.

projects.title: Numeric Precision & Quantization
projects.description: Explore fp32/fp16/bf16/int8 numeric formats, implement symmetric int8 quantization, benchmark GEMM throughput across dtypes on GPU, and implement a mixed-precision forward pass with torch.autocast.

projects.title: Profile a Model's Forward Pass
projects.description: Build a decoder-only mini transformer, profile its forward pass with the PyTorch profiler, compute MFU, classify the top bottlenecks using the roofline model, and produce a written optimization agenda for Phase 2.

phases.title: GPU Kernel Engineering for ML
phases.goal: Write the kernels behind deep learning: optimized GEMM and tensor cores, elementwise/activation kernels, and reductions like softmax and LayerNorm — analyzed with the roofline.

projects.title: Elementwise & Activation Kernels
projects.description: Write ReLU, GELU, sigmoid, add, and scale kernels using grid-stride loops and float4 vectorization, then benchmark each in GB/s against the GPU's peak memory bandwidth to confirm they are bandwidth-limited.

projects.title: GEMM for ML
projects.description: Count FLOPs for real transformer layers, implement a tiled GEMM kernel benchmarked in GFLOP/s vs the GPU peak, and compare against cuBLAS to understand what register tiling, double-buffering, and tensor cores contribute.

projects.title: Tensor Cores & Mixed Precision
projects.description: Write a minimal Tensor Core GEMM using nvcuda::wmma (FP16 inputs, FP32 accumulate), measure the TFLOP/s multiple over FP32 CUDA cores, and compare to cuBLAS HGEMM to understand what the remaining gap requires.

projects.title: Softmax — A Reduction Kernel
projects.description: Implement a numerically stable, block-parallel softmax kernel using shared memory tree reduction and warp shuffles, benchmark it in GB/s, and validate output against a CPU reference to understand the reduction pattern that underlies FlashAttention.

projects.title: LayerNorm & Normalization Kernels
projects.description: Implement LayerNorm using two-pass (mean then variance), Welford one-pass, and fused affine variants, plus RMSNorm, measuring bandwidth improvement across implementations and validating correctness with identity affine parameters.

projects.title: Memory Optimization for ML Kernels
projects.description: Apply coalescing fixes, shared memory staging, float4/half2 vectorized loads, and occupancy tuning to ML kernels, measuring the bandwidth improvement from each technique and assembling them into an optimized LayerNorm.

projects.title: Roofline Analysis of ML Kernels
projects.description: Compute arithmetic intensities for all Phase 2 kernels, place them on the GPU roofline model, run Nsight Compute on at least one kernel, and produce an optimization priority matrix based on each kernel's distance from its theoretical ceiling.

projects.title: An ML Kernel Mini-Library
projects.description: Assemble optimized ReLU, GELU, softmax, LayerNorm, RMSNorm, and tiled GEMM kernels into a structured CUDA library with a clean C++ header interface, a correctness test suite against CPU references, and a benchmark table reporting each kernel's % of theoretical peak bandwidth or compute.

phases.title: Kernel Fusion & FlashAttention
phases.goal: Beat the memory wall with fusion: why fusion wins, fusing elementwise+reductions, online softmax, and a tiled FlashAttention-style fused attention kernel that never materializes the score matrix.

projects.title: Why Fusion Matters
projects.description: Measure the HBM round-trip penalty of an unfused 3-kernel pipeline vs a fused kernel and explain the memory wall that kernel fusion addresses.

projects.title: Fusing Elementwise Chains
projects.description: Fuse bias-add + GELU + scale into a single CUDA kernel, eliminate intermediate HBM round-trips, and measure the bandwidth and latency win on transformer FFN-scale tensors.

projects.title: Fusing Reductions with Elementwise
projects.description: Fuse LayerNorm's two-pass reduction+normalization into a single kernel using shared memory, eliminating one full HBM read of the input tensor.

projects.title: Online (Streaming) Softmax
projects.description: Derive and implement the running-max / running-sum rescaling trick that computes numerically stable softmax over blocks without seeing all elements first — the mathematical core of FlashAttention.

projects.title: Naive Attention on the GPU
projects.description: Implement 3-kernel naive attention (QK^T → softmax → V), measure the O(N²) score-matrix memory footprint, and observe the GPU OOM boundary that motivates FlashAttention.

projects.title: The FlashAttention Idea
projects.description: Study and implement the IO-aware FlashAttention algorithm: tile Q/K/V to fit in SRAM, use online softmax running stats, and accumulate output without ever materializing the N×N score matrix.

projects.title: Implementing a Fused Attention Kernel
projects.description: Implement a working tiled fused single-head attention CUDA kernel using shared memory tiles and the online softmax recurrence, verify against naive attention, and measure peak memory and latency.

projects.title: Fused Attention Benchmark Lab
projects.description: Benchmark fused vs naive attention across sequence lengths 512–8192, measure O(N) vs O(N²) HBM scaling empirically, profile with Nsight Compute, and produce a capstone results table.

phases.title: Triton — GPU Programming in Python
phases.goal: Program GPUs at the block level in Triton: the programming model, writing vector-add/softmax/matmul kernels, autotuning, and why Triton sits above hand-tuned CUDA.

projects.title: Triton — GPU Programming in Python
projects.description: Understand the motivation for Triton (the CUDA productivity wall), the block-level programming model, and set up a working Triton environment on Colab; run a minimal @triton.jit kernel that introduces program_id, tl.arange, tl.load, tl.store, and the launch grid.

projects.title: Your First Triton Kernel — Vector Add
projects.description: Implement element-wise vector addition in Triton end-to-end: write the @triton.jit kernel with tl.program_id / tl.arange / tl.load / tl.store / mask, write the Python driver, verify against PyTorch for both power-of-2 and non-power-of-2 sizes, and benchmark bandwidth against torch.add.

projects.title: Fused Softmax in Triton
projects.description: Implement a row-wise numerically stable softmax kernel in Triton (one program per row, in-kernel tl.max and tl.sum reductions, BLOCK_SIZE = next_power_of_2(n_cols)), verify against torch.softmax, and benchmark to demonstrate 2.5–3x speedup over naive unfused PyTorch.

projects.title: Matrix Multiply in Triton
projects.description: Implement a tiled float32 GEMM in Triton: 2D program grid with pid_m/pid_n, tl.dot for tile MAC, accumulator register tile, pointer arithmetic with 2D masking; verify against torch.matmul and benchmark TFLOP/s toward cuBLAS-class throughput.

projects.title: Autotuning Kernels
projects.description: Add @triton.autotune with a 12-config search space (BM/BN/BK × num_warps × num_stages) to the matmul kernel, observe the autotuner's first-call search and cache behavior, inspect the winning config, and measure 20–50% TFLOP/s improvement over the fixed-config baseline.

projects.title: Fused Attention in Triton
projects.description: Implement a FlashAttention-style single-headed forward attention kernel in Triton: tiled Q/K/V loads, online softmax update (running max + running sum rescaling), running output accumulator; verify against a reference torch implementation and benchmark against naive three-op PyTorch and F.scaled_dot_product_attention.

projects.title: Triton vs CUDA — The Tradeoffs
projects.description: Conduct a structured productivity and performance comparison between Triton and CUDA across four implemented algorithms, analyze Triton's expressibility limits, observe Inductor-generated Triton via torch.compile, and articulate a personal decision framework for when each tool is appropriate.

projects.title: Triton Kernel Lab — Phase 4 Finale
projects.description: Implement and autotune a fused LayerNorm forward kernel in Triton (one program per row, tl.sum for mean and variance, in-register normalization and affine transform), verify against torch.layer_norm, and produce a three-way benchmark table comparing Triton vs torch.layer_norm vs naive 4-op PyTorch.

phases.title: ML Compilers — MLIR, TVM & Graph Optimization
phases.goal: Rise to the durable layer: computational graphs, operator fusion and lowering, MLIR dialects, TVM and torch.compile, and how a model becomes hardware instructions.

projects.title: Computational Graphs
projects.description: Trace a PyTorch model to a torch.fx graph and inspect every node, edge, and data-flow dependency — learning why the graph representation is the foundation that makes all ML compiler optimization possible.

projects.title: Graph-Level Optimizations
projects.description: Implement Dead-Code Elimination, Common-Subexpression Elimination, and constant folding as torch.fx graph passes, then demonstrate operator fusion — reducing a 7-node raw graph to 4 nodes while preserving exact semantics.

projects.title: torch.compile & TorchInductor
projects.description: Compile a transformer FFN block with torch.compile, measure the eager-vs-compiled speedup, inspect the generated Triton kernel via TORCH_LOGS, and diagnose and fix a graph break — learning the full torch.compile production workflow.

projects.title: MLIR: The Multi-Level IR
projects.description: Learn MLIR's dialect system and progressive lowering by tracing a matrix multiply from the high-level linalg dialect through affine loops, GPU launch ops, and NVVM down to PTX — understanding why every serious ML compiler (Triton, IREE, XLA) is built on this infrastructure.

projects.title: Apache TVM & Auto-Scheduling
projects.description: Define a fused ReLU+scale operation as a Tensor Expression, write naive and optimized schedules (fused + vectorized + parallel), measure the speedup, and understand how TVM's Ansor auto-scheduler searches the schedule space to target any hardware from one model description.

projects.title: Lowering & Code Generation
projects.description: Trace the complete lowering pipeline from a PyTorch matmul and softmax through TorchInductor's Triton codegen, illustrative PTX, and down to GPU SASS — understanding what performance decisions are made at each lowering stage and why tiling is the central one.

projects.title: The Compiler Layer as the Durable Edge
projects.description: Analyze the automation trajectory from hand-written CUDA to compiler-generated kernels, map the skills required at the largest AI and platform companies roles to your current capabilities, and produce a concrete 6-month roadmap toward a role at the compiler/architecture layer.

projects.title: Compiler Optimization Lab
projects.description: Take a transformer block (self-attention + FFN), run it eager vs torch.compile vs max-autotune, capture the generated Triton kernels, identify every fusion decision, quantify memory bandwidth savings, and produce a complete compiler analysis report — a portfolio-quality artifact demonstrating Phase 5 mastery.

phases.title: Inference Optimization & the Fused-Attention Capstone
phases.goal: Optimize real inference (KV-cache, quantization, batching, serving engines) and build the capstone: a fused attention kernel measured against a vendor baseline.

projects.title: Inference vs Training
projects.description: Quantify the memory, compute, and bandwidth constraints that make inference a distinct engineering discipline from training, measuring TTFT and TPOT on a small decoder-only transformer and deriving why decode is memory-bandwidth-bound.

projects.title: The KV-Cache
projects.description: Implement multi-head attention with and without KV-cache in PyTorch, verify numerical equivalence, and compute the memory footprint of the cache for production LLMs to understand why PagedAttention was necessary.

projects.title: Quantization for Inference
projects.description: Implement INT8 and INT4 group quantization from scratch, measure quantization error vs FP16 reference, compute the bandwidth win during memory-bound decode, and understand GPTQ and AWQ's activation-aware strategies.

projects.title: Batching & Serving
projects.description: Simulate static vs continuous batching schedulers, derive the arithmetic intensity vs batch size curve, measure real throughput scaling on a small decoder-only transformer, and build a capacity planning tool showing the compounding benefit of quantization plus continuous batching.

projects.title: Inference Engines & Runtimes
projects.description: Profile naive PyTorch inference to identify kernel launch and memory overhead, apply torch.compile to fuse operators, compare TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, llama.cpp, and ONNX Runtime, and build a decision framework for choosing the right engine.

projects.title: Optimizing an End-to-End Model
projects.description: Apply the full inference optimization stack (FP16, torch.compile, INT8 quantization, KV-cache, batching) to a small decoder-only transformer-scale transformer and produce a complete optimization ladder table measuring TTFT, TPOT, throughput, and memory at each stage.

projects.title: The AI-Chip Landscape & Your Path
projects.description: Map the AI-chip ecosystem (NVIDIA, AMD, a hyperscaler TPU, a deterministic-dataflow chip startup, a wafer-scale chip startup, a RISC-V dataflow chip startup, a reconfigurable-dataflow chip startup), understand the CUDA→Triton→MLIR skill ladder, identify frontier-lab roles and their signals, and build a 90-day career plan.

projects.title: Fused Attention Kernel (Track Capstone)
projects.description: Implement scaled-dot-product attention in CUDA (naive baseline), then a FlashAttention-style fused tiled kernel using the online softmax algorithm that never materializes the N×N score matrix. Implement a Triton version as the second implementation. Verify numerical correctness against PyTorch's F.scaled_dot_product_attention. Benchmark latency and peak GPU memory across sequence lengths (512–4096) against the naive baseline and PyTorch SDPA. Explain the speedup and memory savings in memory-traffic terms. Package with reproducible setup, correctness test, and a WRITEUP.md with two key tradeoffs.
